newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus central bank seeks new govt borrowing limit.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus central bank seeks new govt borrowing limit.

text.p: The Cyprus central bank and the finance ministry want to reduce the maximum limit for borrowing by the government from the central bank, the bank's governor said on Friday.
Afxentis Afxentiou said the move was in line with European Union requirements to phase out the privileged access of governments to public funds.
At present the government can source up to 38 percent of its borrowing from central bank advances, up to 43 percent from treasury bills and up to 25 percent from development bonds.
Legislation, which needs parliamentary approval, would cut those ceilings by two percentage points for advances and treasury bills and by five percentage points for development bonds.
"The gradual reduction is an institutional framework (of the EU) which Cyprus has to adjust to," Afxentiou told members of the House finance committee reviewing the bill.

Cyprus is due to start accession talks with the EU in about a year's time. The government says that by then it will have deregulated its interest rate ceiling of nine percent and liberalised foreign exchange flows.
According to the most recent statistics available, the government is comfortably below the proposed borrowing limits.
At December 1995 its debt totalled 3.22 billion pounds ($6.85 billion), of which 360 million was in advances, 282 million in treasury bills and 29 million in development bonds. ($=0.47 pounds)
